newsitem.title: HUNGARY: Hungary's BUX eases after reaching trading high.
newsitem.headline: Hungary's BUX eases after reaching trading high.

text.p: Hungarian shares closed lower on Tuesday as foreign investors were on the sidelines waiting to see what will happen on the Czech market, traders said.
"Foreigners took a wait-and-see stance," said Zsolt Madacsi of ING Barings. "For the time being they do not want to participate too actively."
"Now they focus on the Czech market... but this doesn't mean they would show less interest in the region," he added.
The BUX index finished at 5,973.37 points, down 17.95, from Monday and below a new trading peak of 6,012.20 points. Spot share turnover totalled 2.58 billion forints.
The Czech crown has been under pressure because of short-sellings in the past two weeks, and in a fresh step the Czech central bank allowed the currency to float.
Analysts agreed that the future of the Czech crown remained a factor for the Budapest bourse.
They said that some investors considered reducing their exposure in the eastern European region while others shifted money to other markets within the region.
However, macroeconomic conditions and corporate earnings are in favour of Hungary even though the Hungarian stock market is not very cheap, they said.
"The Hungarian market seems to be avoiding too much influence (from the Czech developments)," said Roger Monson, chief equity strategist at Daiwa Europe in London.
"People percieve that some of the trade deficit problems facing the Czech market and to some extent Poland, probably have been mastered in terms of risk of a crisis in Hungary."

"They also see a gradually improving trend of the economic outlook whereas the risk in the Czech economy seems that there may be further slowdown in the near term," Monson said, adding that Hungarian companies' earnings trend seemed to be solid.
On Tuesday the bourse opened firmer benefiting from higher opening prices for Hungarian Global Depositary Receipts on the SEAQ, but mixed orders pulled the market off a new intraday high.
The pharmaceuticals stocks traded mixed, with Richter closing 95 forints higher after positive recommendations by ING Barings and ABN AMRO Hoare Govett.
Egis, for which ING Barings downgraded its 1997 EPS forecast, gave up 200 forints to end at 11,400.
Elsewhere on the market, the chemicals also closed mixed, with BorsodChem adding 25 forints to 6,505, and TVK losing 25 forints to 2,725.
Tile manufacturer Zalakeramia gave up 20 forints to end at 6,980, after ABN AMRO Hoare Govett downgraded to "hold" from "buy" while New York Broker Budapest revised to "buy" from "sell".
